subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Adrenal gland and endocrine pancreas anatomy
vignette: A developmental biologist is tracing the embryonic origins of the adrenal gland. She observes that the outer cortex and the inner medulla arise from different germ layers and give rise to different classes of hormones.
question: The adrenal medulla is derived from which of the following embryonic cell populations?
explanation_correct: The adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells and is composed of chromaffin cells that secrete the catecholamines epinephrine and norepinephrine. By contrast, the adrenal cortex is derived from mesoderm. This difference in origin underlies the distinct hormone classes produced by the two parts of the gland.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mesoderm gives rise to the adrenal cortex, not the medulla.
explanation_incorrect.B: Endoderm gives rise to thyroid follicular cells and pancreatic islet cells, not the adrenal medulla.
explanation_incorrect.C: Oral ectoderm (Rathke pouch) forms the anterior pituitary, not the adrenal medulla.
explanation_incorrect.E: Hypothalamic neuroectoderm gives rise to the posterior pituitary and hypothalamic neurons, not the adrenal medulla.

educationalObjective: The adrenal medulla arises from neural crest (chromaffin cells), whereas the adrenal cortex arises from mesoderm.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Adrenal gland and endocrine pancreas anatomy
vignette: A student uses the mnemonic "salt, sugar, sex" to remember the three zones of the adrenal cortex and the hormone classes they produce. She is asked to identify which layer is responsible for cortisol secretion.
question: Which zone of the adrenal cortex produces glucocorticoids such as cortisol?
explanation_correct: The three layers of the adrenal cortex follow the GFR mnemonic: Zona Glomerulosa produces mineralocorticoids (salt), Zona Fasciculata produces glucocorticoids (sugar), and Zona Reticularis produces androgens (sex). Cortisol is a glucocorticoid and is therefore a product of the zona fasciculata.

explanation_incorrect.B: The zona glomerulosa produces mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone and is regulated primarily by angiotensin II.
explanation_incorrect.C: The zona reticularis produces androgens such as DHEA, not cortisol.
explanation_incorrect.D: The adrenal medulla produces catecholamines (epinephrine and norepinephrine), not corticosteroids.
explanation_incorrect.E: The capsule is a connective tissue covering and has no hormone-producing role.

educationalObjective: GFR: zona Glomerulosa makes mineralocorticoids, zona Fasciculata makes glucocorticoids (cortisol), and zona Reticularis makes androgens.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Adrenal gland and endocrine pancreas anatomy
vignette: A patient with renal artery stenosis has activation of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. A student is asked which cortical zone is the target of the circulating angiotensin II that drives aldosterone release.
question: Angiotensin II primarily stimulates hormone secretion from which zone of the adrenal cortex?
explanation_correct: Angiotensin II is the primary regulator of the zona glomerulosa, which secretes the mineralocorticoid aldosterone. This is the efferent limb of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. In contrast, the zona fasciculata and zona reticularis are regulated mainly by ACTH and CRH.

explanation_incorrect.A: The zona fasciculata is regulated predominantly by ACTH/CRH and produces glucocorticoids, not primarily by angiotensin II.
explanation_incorrect.B: The zona reticularis is regulated predominantly by ACTH/CRH and produces androgens.
explanation_incorrect.D: The adrenal medulla is regulated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers, not by angiotensin II.
explanation_incorrect.E: The capsule is a connective tissue layer with no endocrine secretory function.

educationalObjective: Angiotensin II regulates the zona glomerulosa (aldosterone), whereas ACTH/CRH regulate the zona fasciculata and reticularis.

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Adrenal gland and endocrine pancreas anatomy
vignette: An immunostained section of a pancreatic islet shows insulin-producing cells clustered centrally, glucagon-producing cells arranged around the periphery, and somatostatin-producing cells scattered between them. A student must match each cell type to its hormone and location.
question: Which of the following correctly matches an islet cell type with its hormone and characteristic intraislet location?
explanation_correct: The islets of Langerhans arise from pancreatic buds and contain alpha cells (glucagon, peripheral), beta cells (insulin, central), and delta cells (somatostatin, interspersed). Thus beta cells producing insulin in the central region is the correct match. Remembering the layout helps link each hormone to its cellular source.

explanation_incorrect.A: Alpha cells produce glucagon and reside peripherally; insulin is a beta-cell product.
explanation_incorrect.B: Beta cells produce insulin and are located centrally, not glucagon-producing peripheral cells.
explanation_incorrect.C: Delta cells produce somatostatin and are interspersed, not insulin-producing central cells.
explanation_incorrect.D: Somatostatin is produced by delta cells, not alpha cells, which produce glucagon.

educationalObjective: Islet alpha cells make glucagon (peripheral), beta cells make insulin (central), and delta cells make somatostatin (interspersed).

subject: Endocrine
subtopic: Adrenal gland and endocrine pancreas anatomy
vignette: A patient has episodic hypertension, palpitations, and diaphoresis caused by a tumor arising in the inner portion of the adrenal gland. Laboratory testing shows markedly elevated catecholamines. A student is asked about the cell type and embryonic origin involved.
question: Which of the following best characterizes the hormone product and embryonic origin of the cell type affected in this tumor?

options.text: Insulin-secreting cells derived from pancreatic buds
Catecholamine-secreting chromaffin cells derived from neural crest
T3/T4-secreting follicular cells derived from endoderm

explanation_correct: The adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest and consists of chromaffin cells that synthesize and secrete the catecholamines epinephrine and norepinephrine in response to preganglionic sympathetic stimulation. A tumor of these cells causes episodic hypertension, palpitations, and sweating. The cortex, by contrast, is mesoderm-derived and secretes steroids.

explanation_incorrect.A: Cortisol is a glucocorticoid produced by the mesoderm-derived zona fasciculata of the cortex, not by the medulla.
explanation_incorrect.B: Insulin-secreting beta cells arise from pancreatic buds and are endodermal in origin, not from the adrenal gland.
explanation_incorrect.C: Aldosterone is a mineralocorticoid produced by the mesoderm-derived zona glomerulosa of the cortex, not by the medulla.
explanation_incorrect.E: T3 and T4 are produced by endodermal thyroid follicular cells, not by cells of the adrenal medulla.

educationalObjective: The neural crest–derived adrenal medulla contains catecholamine-secreting chromaffin cells, distinct from the mesoderm-derived steroid-producing cortex.
